body.statement:
On the fixed pre- and post-treatment grids, suppose the latent-factor restrictions used by Han and Shah~\cite{HanShah2025SSC}, Theorems~1--2 and Appendix~E, can be written
\[
 M=VU_0,\qquad y=v_n^\top U_0,\qquad B=VU_1,
\]
where \(V\in\mathbb R^{N_0\times d}\), \(U_0\in\mathbb R^{d\times T_0}\), \(U_1\in\mathbb R^{d\times J}\), and \(v_n\in\mathbb R^d\).  Write their unit-factor-span condition as \(v_n^\top=w^\top V\) for some \(w\in\mathbb R^{N_0}\), and their post/pre time-factor-span condition as \(U_1=U_0A\) for some \(A\in\mathbb R^{T_0\times J}\).  If \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\), then
\[
 y\in\operatorname{row}(M),\qquad
 yM_r^+B=yA=v_n^\top U_1.
\]
Thus the observed-law spectral functional equals the latent untreated target-post grid on this fixed-grid subclass.  Moreover, the rational law \(P^\star\) in Definition~\ref{def:rational-witness} satisfies these factor/span restrictions by taking \(d=2\), \(V=I_2\), \(U_0=M\), \(U_1=B\), \(A=M^{-1}B\), and \(v_n^\top=yM^{-1}\); for that law the common value is \(\theta=(3/5,3/10)\).
body.proof_tex:
The unit-factor-span condition and the three factorization identities give, equation by equation,
\[
 y=v_n^\top U_0=w^\top VU_0=w^\top M.
\]
Hence \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)\), which proves the first conclusion.  By Assumption~\ref{ass:exact-rank}, \(\operatorname{rank}(M)=r\), so the rank-\(r\) truncation of \(M\) is \(M\) itself and \(M_r^+=M^+\).

To verify the projector identity needed below rather than assume it, take a thin singular-value decomposition \(M=U\Sigma R^\top\), where \(U^\top U=R^\top R=I_r\) and every diagonal entry of \(\Sigma\) is positive.  Then
\[
 M^+=R\Sigma^{-1}U^\top,
 \qquad M^+M=RR^\top.
\]
Because \(y\in\operatorname{row}(M)=\operatorname{row}(R^\top)\), there is a row \(b^\top\in\mathbb R^{1\times r}\) such that \(y=b^\top R^\top\).  Consequently,
\[
 yM^+M=b^\top R^\top RR^\top=b^\top R^\top=y.
\]
The post/pre time-factor-span condition now yields
\[
 B=VU_1=VU_0A=MA.
\]
Combining the last two displays gives
\[
 yM_r^+B=yM^+MA=yA
   =v_n^\top U_0A=v_n^\top U_1,
\]
which proves the fixed-grid embedding.  Notice that the equality to the latent untreated post grid follows from the displayed factor and span restrictions; it is not created by defining the observed-law functional.

For the final assertion, Definition~\ref{def:rational-witness} gives
\[
 M=\begin{pmatrix}4/5&3/5\\3/5&3/10\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 y=(7/10,9/20),
 \qquad
 B=\begin{pmatrix}7/10&2/5\\1/2&1/5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Direct calculation gives
\[
 \det(M)=\frac45\frac3{10}-\frac35\frac35=-\frac3{25}\ne0,
 \qquad yM^{-1}=(1/2,1/2).
\]
Thus \(M\) has rank two.  With \(V=I_2\), \(U_0=M\), \(U_1=B\), \(A=M^{-1}B\), and \(v_n^\top=yM^{-1}\), one has
\[
 VU_0=M,\qquad v_n^\top U_0=y,
 \qquad VU_1=B,
 \qquad U_0A=MM^{-1}B=B=U_1,
\]
and the unit-factor span holds with \(w=v_n\).  Finally,
\[
 v_n^\top U_1=(1/2,1/2)
 \begin{pmatrix}7/10&2/5\\1/2&1/5\end{pmatrix}
 =(3/5,3/10)=\theta.
\]
This proves that the witness belongs to the same fixed-grid factor/span subclass.
body.justification: The proposition embeds Han and Shah's fixed-grid latent-factor conditions into the row-space and exact-transport restrictions used by the spectral theorem, rather than merely asserting that the two setups coincide.
body.gap: Han and Shah (2025, Theorems 1--2 and Appendix E) provide the factor and PCR architecture; the proposition records the exact matrix bridge to the row-donor orientation used here and verifies that the rational Kaplan--Meier/PCR witness remains inside that structural subclass.
body.consumer: The bridge supplies the fixed-grid targeting map for the untreated United States post-treatment curve when the stated Han--Shah spans hold. In the 925-patient, 10-country TCL application, inference based on that map could be used only if this note's within-cell i.i.d., cross-cell independence, censoring, covariance, and learner conditions are separately verified; the algebraic bridge does not establish them.
